item.title: Mass Effect 3’s Co-op Multiplayer Is Revived with Legendary Edition Multiplayer Mod on N7 Day, Even as BioWare’s Closure Hangs Over the Celebration
item.description:
2026's N7 Day may be sad (albeit with a tinge of hope provided by a Canadian petition to the government ) for Mass Effect fans following BioWare 's closure, but the ME3Tweaks group (the same folks behind the Pinnacle Station and Happy Ending mods, for example) have a long-awaited gift in store for the community: Legendary Edition Multiplayer , now available for download on Nexus Mods.

As you can easily guess, it is the Mass Effect 3 multiplayer ported to 2021's Legendary Edition , which included the entire original trilogy but skipped the cooperative multiplayer mode that BioWare had introduced with the third installment.

In a blog post that Wccftech received in advance of the release, the modders go in depth into the making of this huge project. Codenamed ' Milan ', Legendary Edition Multiplayer took the ME3Tweaks group three years to make. In April 2026, the team decided to split it off entirely from the Legendary Edition; you'll still need to own LE, but the multiplayer mod won't otherwise interact with it in any way.

The mod, however, does not merely port the original mode for ME3; there are many improvements , including:

  • Field of View (FOV)
  • Aim Assist Tweaks/Configurable Aim Assist
  • Full controller support
  • Private servers (host your own) with one-click invites/mid match invites
  • Photo mode/spectator
  • Ultrawide monitor support
  • Clean base (depends on LE, with integration to pull achievements from LE to unlock cosmetic items)
  • Upscaled textures (some redrawn, most upscaled)
  • Rebaked lighting
  • Mesh improvements
  • Loads of bug fixes
  • MP status icons
  • Heavy weapons
  • New wavelist modes (Unified, Coalition)

The ME3Tweaks group also made other internal changes to support future expansion of Legendary Edition Multiplayer, such as increasing the maximum number of supported maps from 30 to 255 . Indeed, they will release a mod maker for community use while continuing to work on additions such as the Redemption Map Pack and Rejection .

The former is a remake of the original map pack created by one of the group's members; the new version will feature proper lighting, pathing, and fewer networking issues . The modders also hope to add a brand new map with working cover. As for Rejection, it would also be a reimplementation of the original mod , which added several new enemies to multiplayer mode. The mod was prototyped but has not yet received a network playtest, and it may take a while to fix the inevitable issues.

The ME3Tweaks group has also done work to make creating new "kits" (character classes, essentially) much easier. Moreover, several minor improvements are already planned , such as improving in-game text chat, improving blind firing, replacing the Challenges interface and the downed UI, and enabling configuration of lobby sizes.

Lastly, the modders disclosed their use of AI , which had been nonexistent for the first two years of development. However, in the last few months, they leveraged AI tools for bug fixing, UI prototyping, pipeline performance, and feature research, which is pretty normal nowadays.

item.title: Dual RTX PRO 6000 GPUs Worth $32,000 Narrowly Escape Catastrophic Meltdown Thanks To The Owner’s Early Visual Inspection, Says Frayed 12V-2×6 Cables Raised Alarm
item.description:
NVIDIA’s RTX PRO 6000 might cost $16,000 a pop , but for running top-end local AI models, it’s a PC builder’s dream, and when you have two units running at a time, there’s really no need to give companies like OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and others your hard-earned cash. However, since these GPUs cost as much as a brand-spanking-new sedan, it’s imperative that you monitor their operations closely. One owner did, and that’s exactly how he potentially saved both of his RTX PRO 6000 units, as the frayed 12V-2x6 cables were caught before any irreparable harm could be done.

Crumbling 12V-2x6 wire sleeving across dual RTX PRO 6000 graphics cards indicates substantial thermal wear

The alarming case surfaced on the r/PcBuild subreddit, where user ‘u/Doomslayer606’ shared close-up photos prominently showing degraded 12V-2x6 power cables. Both of the RTX PRO 6000 GPUs were paired with a top-of-the-line Seasonic PRIME TX-1600 Noctua Edition power supply because running two workstation-class graphics cards necessitates a beefy PSU. During a physical inspection of the workstation interior, the owner noticed that the braided fabric wrapping individual wires was literally coming apart right at the terminal heads.

As shown in the images, the outer braided sleeving on two specific power leads directly behind the 600W connector shows significant heavy thermal wear. The fabric clearly looks frayed, pale, and discolored. Furthermore, the Redditor confirmed that the wear wasn’t confined to a single wire or even a single card, as both 12V-2x6 cables exhibited identical degradation at both the GPU and PSU ends. However, one cable suffered significantly more visible decay than the other.

While the underlying inner wire insulation and the plastic connector shells showed no outward signs of damage or scorching, the physical condition suggests an internal current imbalance. Obviously, under sustained dual GPU compute workloads, even the slightest seating tolerances or contact resistance can cause the current to unevenly skew across the six 12V lines. This disparity caused immense heat output, resulting in the damage materialized in the images.

The owner should consider himself lucky that he spotted the damage before something catastrophic transpired; otherwise, he’d be looking at a hefty GPU bill. Even if he could afford a dual RTX PRO 6000 purchase again, it’s not like these workstation GPUs are widely available, as the DRAM shortage has applied a ‘chokehold’ on the chip supply, with data centers gobbling up the available units.

The user confirmed they are replacing both cables immediately rather than risking further operation. For anyone operating high TDP hardware or multi-GPU configurations, this incident serves as an essential reminder: catching brittle, discolored, or frayed wire sleeving early can prevent an eventual short circuit or terminal meltdown that could destroy hardware worth thousands of dollars.

The Redditor has confirmed that he’ll be replacing both cables, since that’s the prudent approach. As for the others rocking similar hardware or RTX 5090 units, you should pay attention to the 12V-2x6 cables as well as the 12V-2x6 16-pin power connector, since these are prone to melting .

News Source: Reddit

item.title: Mass Effect’s N7 Day Follows EA Shutting Down BioWare and Canceling Its Next Game, but Fans’ Petition Will Force the Canadian Government to Respond
item.description:
Today is N7 Day , the annual day that celebrates BioWare's Mass Effect franchise. This year, though, it might very well be the saddest N7 Day to date, given that the studio was just shut down by Electronic Arts and its new Mass Effect Universe game was canceled as part of that process, with the publisher choosing to fund Star Wars Battlefront 3 instead.

As someone once said in a beloved movie trilogy, though, there is still hope. Global fans have been pouring their love through the Change.org petition , which is now closing in on 310K signatures , but it is a smaller petition that might carry the greatest potential to save the studio.

BioWare is a Canadian studio headquartered in Edmonton, Alberta. Back in 2018, its original founders, the doctors Greg Zeschuk and Ray Muzyka , were even awarded the Order of Canada , one of the country's highest honors, for the developer's revolutionary impact on videogames. As you might recall, New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis had publicly called for the government to save the historic developer ; now, following petition e-7898, initiated by citizen Brendan Routh and now carrying over 4800 signatures, the government will indeed have to give an official response.

In Canada, once an electronic petition has at least 500 valid signatures from citizens or residents, it becomes certified, and the petitioner's Member of Parliament can then present it to the government. Unsurprisingly, the Member of Parliament championing this cause is Don Davies of Lewis's New Democratic Party, who wrote on BlueSky :

BioWare’s US parent company, EA, has decided to close the studio. These publishers buy developers, run them into the ground, and rip them apart for profit. There's a pattern of US companies buying Canadian businesses and shutting them down, costing Canadians their jobs. The developers at BioWare know how to run their studio. They know how to make the games that fans love. They should be given the first opportunity – and the federal support – to buy it and run it themselves. If you agree, sign the petition!

The petition itself asks the following:

  1. Provide BioWare with the capital necessary to secure independence of themselves and their intellectual property from Electronic Arts and resume business as an independent, Canadian company;
  2. Protect Canadian businesses and cultural institutions from being dictated by American and foreign corporate interests; and
  3. Champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights at the centre of Canada's national identity by preserving BioWare's invaluable contribution to the global entertainment industry.

Of course, there's no guarantee the government will accept it , given the amount of funding it would require. Still, the hope is alive, and that's enough for now.

As a side note, Deadline reported two days ago that a video documentary of BioWare's final days, called Massive Effect: The Bioware Story , is being produced by filmmakers Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie and will air on Canada's Super Channel . The timing was fortuitous: the crew began filming the documentary two years ago and continued up until the news of the closure, thus capturing that crucial and sad moment from the inside.

item.title: Intel Razor Lake-S Desktop CPUs Reportedly Arrive In 2028 On The Same LGA 1954 Socket As Nova Lake-S, Extending Multi-Generational Platform Support
item.description:
Intel's Razor Lake-S Desktop CPUs are reportedly going to arrive in 2028, a year after the launch of Nova Lake-S on the same LGA 1954 platform .

Intel Razor Lake-S Desktop CPUs To Extend Multi-Generational Support On LGA 1954 Platforms

It looks like Intel is preparing a slew of Razor Lake chips for 2028 . While we wait for Nova Lake to launch next year in the form of Nova Lake-S, Nova Lake-HX, and Nova Lake-H configurations, the Razor Lake lineup will span all of these and a higher-end AX configuration, which was talked about last month.

According to Jaykihn at X , Intel's Razor Lake-S Desktop CPUs are still scheduled for a 2028 release. It is not mentioned which quarter we can expect these, but considering the Nova Lake-S is eyeing a Q1 2027 release, Razor Lake-S could launch around Computex 2028 or the second half of 2028.

One of the biggest updates for Razor Lake CPUs will be the upgrade to the Griffin Cove P-Core architecture. This new architecture will be built upon the Coyote Cove P-Core architecture that will be featured on Nova Lake-S CPUs. Earlier information suggested higher core counts, and we can also expect the use of next-generation process technologies.

Griffin Cove P-Cores will also be deployed on the next-gen Xeon family codenamed Coral Rapids , and while that features SMT support, the client lineup will not feature SMT. Jaykihn states that it will be a similar core with a separate architecture. You can compare these to Coyote Cove and Panther Cove P-Core architectures, per the insider. We know from previous information that a lot of Nova Lake SKUs were moved over to Razor Lake.

On the entry-level side, Intel's Wildcat Lake Refresh "Core Series 4" is targeting a Q2 2027 release with its compute tile based on 18A-P, while Moon Lake will be launching in Q4 2027 with an 18A compute tile. Wildcat Lake Refresh CPUs will stick with Panther Cove P-Cores and Arctic Wolf E-Cores, while Moon Lake will feature Darkmont LPE cores.

Although Intel hasn't announced anything in relation to Nova Lake yet, they have mentioned the lineup multiple times and initially targeted a 2H 2026 release, but latest reports position the lineup as a 1H 2027 launch . The company has been disclosing the preliminary details to its partners, some of which have already been leaked, so we are expecting more information to land in the coming months.

item.title: Intel Panther Lake And Wildcat Lake Chips Land On Maxsun MoDT Motherboards Built For NAS Builds, With Up To 128 GB Of DDR5-7200 Memory
item.description:
Intel Panther Lake & Wildcat Lake MoDT motherboards are arriving soon, targeting the NAS market with a wide array of features.

Maxsun Deploys NAS-Focused Intel Panther Lake & Wildcat Lake MoDT Motherboards

Back at Computex 2026, we spotted the first Intel Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake MoDT designs . These were made by Maxsun and were aimed at the NAS market. Now, Maxsun has shared more information on these two products, which are arriving soon.

The company is preparing two options, one with Intel's Panther Lake "Core Ultra Series 3" SoCs and up to 4+8+4 configurations, and the other with Intel's Wildcat Lake "Core Series 3" SoCs that come in the Core 7 350 option.

Maxsun SK-PTLNAS MoDT Motherboard

For the higher-end SK-PTLNAS, Maxsun is enabling Panther Lake chips up to the Core Ultra 9 386H, which packs 16 CPU cores and 4 Xe3 iGPU cores. The chip has a base power of 25 W & scales up to 80W. Power is provided through an 8-pin CPU and 24-pin ATX connector.

The MoDT motherboard for this design features a white-colored PCB. The VRM design is a 6+4 configuration. There are two SO-DIMM slots for DDR5 capacities of up to 128 GB and speeds of up to 7200 MT/s. There is a full-length PCIe Gen5 x8, and there are five M.2 SSD slots (2x Gen5x2, 2 Gen4x1, 1 Gen4x2). Another SSD slot is located at the top & features support for WIFI modules. There are also three Mini SAS (SFF-8643) ports for additional storage.

The MoDT also comes with a DEBUG LED and onboard buttons for clearing the CMOS. USB ports include dual Thunderbolt Type-C (Display+40 Gbps), two USB 3.2 Gen1 Type-A, and two USB 2.0 ports. Display outputs include an HDMI, a DisplayPort, and an EDP connector. Networking comes in the form of dual 1GbE LAN ports, a single 2.5GbE LAN port, and a 10 GbE LAN port.

Maxsun SK-WCLAIO MoDT Motherboard

The Wildcat Lake option has seen a big update since the last time we saw it. The design has moved to a 90x165mm form factor and now features support for Intel's Core 7 350. This CPU features 6 cores in a 2 P-Core and 4 LPE-Core configuration. It also packs 2 Xe3 iGPU cores with base power rated at 15W and maximum turbo power rated at 35W.

The CPU is powered by a 4+2 phase VRM. Memory options include a single SO-DIMM slot with support for up to 48 GB capacities and 6400 MT/s speeds. Storage includes 1 TB of onboard UFS 3.1 with up to 850 MB/s speeds, and four M.2 M-Key ports. USB options include dual Thunderbolt 4.0 Type-C ports, dual USB 3.0 ports, and dual USB 2.0 ports. The board is powered by a 12V DC Jack, and the maximum supported TDP is 28W.

Maxsun hasn't revealed the prices of these products yet, but the launch is happening this month so stay tuned for more information.

item.title: A Kitchen Slide Manufacturer Controls Up To 90 Percent Of The AI Server Market, Thanks To Precise Manufacturing Of Racks Housing Multi-Million GPU Clusters
item.description:
There’s unprecedented attention on cutting-edge AI chips, data centers, and DRAM, but one of the most overlooked components of this supply chain happens to be the mechanical side of stacking the entire hardware inside. Yes, we’re talking about the physical server racks, and when you think of this paraphernalia, the last company that comes to mind would be a manufacturer responsible for kitchen cabinet drawer slides.

However, here’s the most surprising bit. Taiwanese manufacturer King Slide Works, a company originally known for engineering everyday household drawers, currently commands an estimated 70 to 90 percent market share in precision slide rails used for high-end AI server racks.

Precision engineering and 3,750 patents create an unbreakable moat for high-end AI server rails, and King Slide is happily walking to the bank

A standard server rail operates on the same mechanical principle as a heavy duty kitchen drawer, relying on three steel strips sliding across rows of steel ball bearings, making things rather simple for King Slide when the latter decided to transition to mass manufacturing AI server racks. Unfortunately, it isn’t as simple as it sounds, because the physical constraints imposed by modern AI cabinets require extreme mechanical precision.

For instance, two rails of an AI server node measure just 6.1mm thick, yet when extended fully outward during maintenance, they must suspend a chassis weighing over 40kg without flexing, bending, or jamming, which is a massive challenge. Each rail assembly incorporates over 100 individual components, with dimensional tolerances that cannot deviate by more than a razor-thin 0.02 mm.

The engineering stakes rise even higher when we discuss significantly more powerful architectures like NVIDIA’s Blackwell GB200. While these AI cabinets continue to become heavier, the rails must become thinner to leave physical clearance for high flow liquid cooling equipment and thick coolant plumbing running along the internal rack frame.

That being said, the risk of a single rail failure can result in utter catastrophe where hundreds of thousands of dollars worth of computing hardware crashes to the floor and becomes useless. This sole reason is why hyperscalers and server assemblers refuse to gamble on cheaper alternatives, leaving King Slide to pocket that delicious premium.

The company’s engineering expertise has transformed its business into a gold mine, because, according to statistics shared by Gaurab Chakrabarti , it was revealed that King Slide obtained a staggering 87.4 percent gross margin in Q2 2026, with a rail kit selling for under 100 dollars while protecting equipment valued in the millions. However, replicating these AI server racks shouldn’t be a Herculean task, which is why King Slide has protected its interests.

How? By holding roughly 3,750 patents covering custom stamping lines, plating methods, tooling, and latching mechanisms, creating an almost insurmountable legal and manufacturing barrier to potential rivals. The only time that King Slide faced a modicum of a challenge in this market was when fellow Taiwanese manufacturer Nan Juen entered into the fold in 2002, before finally breaching NVIDIA’s supply chain and becoming a partner for the GB200.

Still, King Slide’s dominance will likely be maintained for the next several years, especially now that they’ve approved more than 600 million dollars in capital expenditure to construct the world’s largest server rail manufacturing plant.

item.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Now Runs at 60 FPS on PC Emulators Lichii and Eglantine, a Day After Booting at 20-30 FPS
item.description:
Yesterday we reported that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was booting on PC at 15 to 30 FPS within hours of its official Switch 2 launch, albeit with heavy visual glitches. Just a day later, the situation has already massively improved.

DSOGaming reports that the Lichii emulator has fixed most of the remake’s visual issues in a single day, with the starting area and the Great Deku Tree now running at 60 FPS rather than the 20-30 FPS of launch day. One user on X went further, describing the latest build as running at a stable 4K 60 FPS with clear visuals , no bloom problem, no artifacts, and no slow motion, with only minor stutters and freezing left.

Separately, a Discord user running a 5700X CPU and RTX 5070 GPU with precompiled shaders reported in the Eglantine server reaching the Kokiri Sword from a new save with texture flickering still present on foliage and ground, a lighting fault on the Great Deku Tree during the opening animation, desynced audio in parts of the first cinematic, and slowdowns from low framerate. Which is roughly where you'd expect a two-day-old compatibility effort to be . Still, their video demonstrates a largely playable game, as you can see in the embed below.

The Eglantine repository shows the frantic activity of the modding team to improve Ocarina of Time compatibility. Lichii is a fork of Eglantine, which itself builds on Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, and Eglantine has pushed two Ocarina-specific test branches in the past day alone .

The fix/oot-blackscreen branch, built early on November 6, fixed those artifacts people have initially experienced . The Vulkan scheduler now pauses rather than resets the occlusion counter at each submission, which was producing the white flashes. Shader work covering nested returns addresses a black scene on AMD hardware. Storage buffers are now bound behind loaded pointers specifically for the game’s vegetation, which the developers’ own notes tie to the white wash some users reported.

A second branch, oot-optimization-fixes, landed around four hours ago and is almost entirely performance work : pipeline caching across sixteen sessions, saving every fifteen seconds; building a pipeline that a draw is actually waiting on rather than queuing it behind others; and building cached pipelines on background threads during boot.

The DLSS Conundrum

As an interesting side note, YouTuber ElAnalistaDeBits has taken a rather different approach to improving the remake's image quality: injecting NVIDIA DLSS via HDMI. The results, he shows, substantially clean up the shimmering that Nintendo’s choice of FSR 1.0 leaves in the native game .

It's a demonstration rather than a fix, of course. The console is still rendering what it always did, and nothing about the capture changes that. But it's a keen one, because the Switch 2's hardware notoriously supports DLSS and third-party developers do use it regularly . Nintendo's own first-party output, including Ocarina of Time, continues to employ FSR 1.0 instead , which is puzzling, to say the least.

There's simply no comparison between AMD FSR 1.0 and even the relatively old DLSS 3.1 CNN model available on the Switch 2 , but Nintendo being Nintendo, they'll just keep doing their own thing without explaining themselves to anyone. Of course, that largely works for them, as seen once again with the excellent reception of this remake .

item.title: Elon Musk Says SpaceX Will Attempt A “Critical Breakthrough Needed To Make Life Multiplanetary,” As Its Government-Derived Revenues Shrink To Just 5% Next Year
item.description:
SpaceX is gearing up to try to retrieve all parts of its orbital rocket in a manner that would render them eminently reusable on multiple missions, significantly ratcheting up the efficiency of its missions.

Meanwhile, Elon Musk has just revealed that SpaceX's exposure to government-derived revenues is all set to shrink to a negligible proportion of its total cash haul by next year, which should dampen the leverage that the Democrats might hold in pursuing retaliatory measures.

Elon Musk: "SpaceX contracts with the government are BOTH the best product AND the lowest price!"

Currently, the Super Heavy booster, which houses 33 Raptor engines, and the Starship upper stage, with 6 Raptors, costs SpaceX roughly $100 million in manufacturing costs, with the upper stage alone costing roughly $40 million .

However, Elon Musk has just announced that SpaceX will now attempt to capture both the Super Heavy booster and the upper stage of the Starship, unlocking immense economies of scale in the process, while constituting "the critical breakthrough needed to make life multiplanetary."

"SpaceX will attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and Starship on the upcoming flight.

If both are successful, it will mark the first time that all parts of an orbital rocket return to Earth intact.

This is the critical breakthrough needed to make life multiplanetary."

By capturing both of these critical components, SpaceX can reduce its per-flight costs to just $2 million to $10 million, with fuel and labor making up the bulk of this range, especially as manufacturing costs will get amortized over dozens of flights - $100 million over 100 flights equates to just $1 million in amortized hardware costs.

Separately, Elon Musk has revealed that SpaceX's government-derived revenue is all set to become a nominal component of its overall revenue mix next year :

"Tesla has no government contracts and President Trump ended federal incentives for electric vehicles.

SpaceX contracts with the government are BOTH the best product AND the lowest price! Moreover government revenue will be less than 10% of SpaceX revenue this quarter and less then 5% a year from now.

Happy to cancel any that the government doesn’t want. Just say the word!"

This issue of perceived government leverage has become a critical matter in the aftermath of Gina Hinojosa's successful bid for the governorship of Texas, a state which is absolutely critical for Tesla and SpaceX but now finds itself, quite atypically, under the rule of the Democrats.

While there is copious bad blood between the Democrats and Musk, whose apex role within the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) only added to the overall acerbity of this relationship, Texas' new Senator-elect, James Talarico, has just expressed surprisingly positive views on Musk and his various ventures , hinting that there might yet be hope for salvaging this relationship.

item.title: GTA 6 Could Cost “Tens of Thousands Of Dollars” in Tokens To Develop Unofficial PC Port, Yet Former Rockstar Tech Director Believes It Will Be Attempted
item.description:
GTA 6 , much like Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 , will launch on PC some time after its PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S launch. However, the rise of generative AI that is making it extremely easy for anyone to port games to PC or improve emulation is likely going to pressure the studio and its parent company Take-Two Interactive into releasing the game officially on PC sooner than expected , as former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij believes some will cross any hurdle to get it on PC as soon as possible, even if it would cost tens of thousands of dollars in tokens.

"It really has changed the world," Vermeij said to Rock Paper Shotgun in a fresh interview, "and I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking."

As GTA 6 is setting out to be an incredibly complex production, an AI-powered PC port won't be an easy feat. Still, Obbe Vermeij believes current tools are probably capable of delivering this port, but at a tremendously high cost in terms of time and money. "It will take a long time. It actually, physically takes hours and hours and hours to do these things. And it will take a bunch of tokens and everything, so it would probably cost like, tens of thousands of dollars in tokens. But like, you know, if it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it," Vermeij said.

Besides being able to play GTA 6 on PC ahead of an official port with features not available on consoles such as NVIDIA DLSS 5 , there could be another reason that could motivate many to release something that would require an unreasonable effort to produce: to spite Sony . In the past few months, the Japanese company had made a series of rather unpopular decisions, such as sunsetting disc production in 2028, fueling the quick development of the KyTyPS5 emulator and unofficial ports of games still stuck on PlayStation consoles, such as FromSoftware's Bloodborne .

Even so, with PlayStation engaging in a firmware war against jailbreakers to prevent GTA 6 from being dumped at launch, chances of the game being playable in some form on PC as soon as it launches like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time are slim. As such, players will have no choice but to play the game on PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S to enjoy what is increasingly looking like one of the most advanced open-world game s to date.

item.title: NVIDIA GPUs Worth $11.4 Million Stolen From Oakland Fetch A Hefty Price Outside Of U.S.; UC Berkeley Professor Says “They Go For About 1 Million Or More Abroad”
item.description:
The astronomical value of NVIDIA’s AI GPUs will attract the wrong kind of attention. Just last month, we reported that an RTX 5090 shipment worth almost $500,000 was stolen from a Brazilian airport . Now, a similar theft has taken place, one where the value of these graphics chips reaches a mammoth $11.4 million. According to the latest report, pallets loaded with NVIDIA hardware mysteriously disappeared while en route to data center facilities in Texas. As for where they’re potentially headed, a UC Berkeley professor thinks they can fetch almost double the price outside of the U.S.

A domestic NVIDIA chip shipment costing $550,000 can reach as high as $1 million when sold, according to the professor

The latest details from ABC7News mention police reports discussing cargo that was picked up as planned by a commercial truck bearing the logo of a food transport company. However, the vehicle dropped off the radar while traveling south out of the Bay Area, and investigators eventually lost track of the truck in San Bernardino County. The crime was formally reported to the Oakland Police Department on September 13, creating a massive time lag that granted the perpetrators ample runway to disperse the hardware

Security and economics experts point out that the immense commercial appetite for AI accelerators has created enormous criminal pressure on vulnerable supply chains. Olaf Groth, a professor at UC Berkeley Haas School of Business, states that “there’s lots and lots of incentives to hijack those chips anywhere where security is weak,” and “these chips command about double the price that they command inside the United States. So, if a chip costs about $550,000, then they go for about 1 million or more abroad.”

Groth referred to these NVIDIA chips as a “national security asset,” and criticized the weak security detail protecting the pricey AI hardware. Also, the scale and complexity of these thefts mean that criminals have had to adapt, evolve, and become more creative in pulling off a heist of this magnitude. The incident is part of an alarming trend of high value technology thefts hitting the Bay Area.

In 2025, law enforcement in Fremont and Union City investigated multiple commercial burglaries involving NVIDIA cargo valued at more than $7.5 million. Thieves have become so aggressive that another crew recently attempted to steal trailers in Fremont, believing they were loaded with expensive NVIDIA hardware, only to discover that the rigs were filled with 40,000 pounds of sand used for braking tests.

Groth warns that these “assets” could easily end up in adversary states like China, and evidence suggests that the country is leveraging various strategies to obtain access to specialized NVIDIA hardware. For instance, it took a security research firm to discover 32 B300 units deployed at China Telecom . This specific AI GPU is currently on the U.S. export control list, meaning that it cannot be shipped to the country through traditional means.

News Source: ABC7News

item.title: Microsoft Learns Its Lesson With Copilot Being Shoved Down The User’s Throat; Promises Optional Addition In Windows 11 Search UI
item.description:
Windows 11’s optimizations don’t just include making the operating system more responsive and more suitable for 8GB RAM systems , but also providing a refined experience for users without forcing them to use or rely on certain features. The company learned this the hard way when its Copilot strategy failed miserably, forcing the software giant to backtrack on its decision and introduce a more subtle approach. Windows 11’s Search UI will be integrated with Copilot, but unlike last time, users can opt out.

Copilot efforts are still being made, but they will be less intrusive

The Windows 11 Search UI redesign represents a direction towards making desktop navigation faster while laying the groundwork for hybrid intelligence across local hardware and cloud systems. The foundation of the rebuilt interface introduces native actions, allowing users to execute system-level controls straight from the query box without needing complex language models or requiring dedicated NPUs.

Small actions like being able to switch to Windows 11’s dark mode, mute audio, and more will help streamline routine desktop tweaks into instant, one-click interactions. Best of all, Microsoft has stated that Copilot will be integrated into Search and is expected to roll out to certain markets before 2026 ends, with the flexibility that users would not be bound to exclusively have it in front of them.

“We will also begin adding the option to integrate the new Copilot with Search on the taskbar, so you can get quick answers inline from Search, and if you want to have a richer conversation, you can jump from Search directly to the full Copilot app. This experience will be opt in, and will first start rolling out to select markets later this year.”

Previously, Copilot would clutter the Taskbar while also utilizing valuable system resources, particularly on low-end systems, so Microsoft is taking a more thoughtful approach to improving Windows 11. Users will also have the flexibility to keep Copilot disabled without losing access to core operating system search improvements.

By treating artificial intelligence as a modular choice rather than an unavoidable requirement, Microsoft may finally strike the right balance between modernizing desktop functionality and respecting traditional PC control. The company followed a similar approach with OneDrive, with users finally being allowed to opt out of the service instead of having to face the incessant reminders. It finally appears that Microsoft has turned over a new leaf.

item.title: Chinese Memory Chip Manufacturer CXMT Struggles In Q3 As Share Drops To 9% Amidst Aggressive Ramp From Samsung, Says Research
item.description:
Chinese memory manufacturer CXMT's market share in the DRAM memory chip industry is coming under pressure as behemoth Samsung scales its production and the market starts to focus on high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips. The latest statistics come courtesy of Counterpoint Research, and they outline that CXMT's market share in the DRAM market grew to 9% in Q3 2026 for a four percentage point jump over the year-ago figure.

Samsung Scales Memory Production & CXMT's DRAM Market Share Slips From 10% To 9% Sequentially In Q3, Says Counterpoint Research

The latest figures from Counterpoint follow the firm's earlier report covering the second quarter, which outlined that China's CXMT was the fastest-growing DRAM manufacturer in the world when it came to revenue. The figures outlined that CXMT's revenue in the second quarter grew by a whopping 716%. In terms of market share, the Chinese company's overall market share in terms of revenue was 7%, while Samsung led the pie with 39% market share in August 2026.

The research firm added that a major reason CXMT's revenue had grown was domestic demand from Chinese companies. Counterpoint also outlined that for CXMT to sustain its growth, it would have to expand production capacity and grow penetration in the domestic and overseas memory chip markets.

In its latest report, covering the third quarter, Counterpoint outlines that CXMT's market share slipped to 9% in Q3 from 10% in Q2. The firm added that Samsung led the pack as it held 38% of the market while SK hynix's market share was 29%. Crucially, compared to the second quarter figures, Samsung's figure grew by five percentage points while SK hynix's share dropped by four points in an environment experiencing a ramp of HBM4 memory chips for the AI buildout.

The reason behind the shift is a higher price mix. In fact, the data shows quite a stark difference, as Counterpoint outlines that while DRAM revenue grew by almost five times on an annual basis, bit shipments jumped by a modest 4%. Specifically, DRAM average selling prices touched $1.9/gigabit.

However, just as agentic AI is reshaping the role of CPUs in the AI buildout, it is also contributing to a resurgence in demand for conventional DRAM. Additionally, the GPU-to-CPU ratio is also narrowing, as it currently sits at 2:1. The dip in the ratio mirrors forecasts by Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who had remarked during the firm's second quarter earnings call that the ratio had dropped from an earlier 8:1 to 4:1 .

item.title: Xbox Is Closer Than Ever to Being Sold Off by Microsoft After Democrats Swept Congress, According to Gaming Industry Analyst Joost van Dreunen
item.description:
Following the so-called Blue Wave that swept through the U.S. Capitol as the Democrats gained control of the entire Congress, gaming industry analyst Joost van Dreunen believes that Xbox is closer than ever to being divested by Microsoft .

In a Substack blog post eloquently titled ' The election that could break up Xbox ' , the former founder of SuperData Research, now a professor at NYU Stern, argues that Democrat voters showed their displeasure with the growing number of data centers being built across the United States . van Dreunen cites a Wall Street Journal report alleging that voters in more than 40 towns and counties considered data center-related ballot measures, with at least 10 approving restrictions or outright bans. Moreover, a nationwide survey of over 79,000 registered voters found that candidates' positions on AI and data centers were a "major" factor in the choices of 56 percent of participants.

How does that relate to Xbox? Well, it's a fact that Microsoft has pushed heavily on building AI infrastructure and did so at a high cost, including studio closures and layoffs at the gaming division . Now, things might get much harder , with some of the newly elected Democratic governors already promising to halt new permits, end tax breaks for new data center construction, and the like.

Xbox might therefore increasingly look like a worthy sacrifice to Microsoft executives , especially as its revenue continues to decline (albeit at a reduced rate), while the Search and Advertising department grew 10% in 2026, greatly outpacing the gaming division.

Just a few weeks ago, the tech business insider website The Information reported that unnamed private equity buyers have already explored the potential acquisition of Xbox from Microsoft, valuing the division at $100 to $150 billion . A Microsoft spokesperson commented on the rumor, saying Xbox is not for sale, but that might change in the near future.

Joost van Dreunen even posits that CEO Asha Sharma 's decision to establish a dedicated ' XP ' department to bring Xbox franchises to other media (chiefly film and television) could make the acquisition even more appealing to certain buyers, as it helps make Xbox look like a traditional entertainment and media company.

Of course, the extent to which the US mid-term election really accelerates Microsoft's divestiture of Xbox remains to be seen; the picture painted by van Dreunen is intriguing, but far from inevitable.

item.title: PlayStation 6 Could End Smurfing in Ranked Games, as Sony Patents a System That Lets Developers Restrict or Ban Secondary Accounts
item.description:
If you have ever played any competitive game, you should be well aware of the smurfing phenomenon that ruins the experience for anyone who isn't a top player. By creating alternate accounts, high-rank players return to the bottom of the competitive ladder, stomping through less experienced players for all sorts of reasons, often not very good ones. However, next-generation systems like the PlayStation 6 may solve this long-standing issue (while also improving cloud gaming ), as Sony has patented new technology to detect players using secondary accounts to make ranked modes in competitive games fairer.

"Systems and methods for using gameplay characteristics to identify a user are provided. A computing system can receive user interaction data corresponding to a first player account of a gaming platform. The user interaction data can be generated by the user associated with the first player account interacting with the gaming platform. The computing system can determine a first set of characteristics of the user interaction data," reads a new patent filed by Sony on April 20 and published on November 5, as reported by Patentlyze .

"The computing system can determine whether the first set of characteristics match a second set of characteristics of different user interaction data associated with a second player account interacting with the gaming platform. Based on determining that the first set of characteristics match the second set of characteristics, the computing system can provide an indication that the first set of characteristics related to the first player account match the second set of characteristics."

Looking at the patent, this new Sony tech works in a rather straightforward way. The system collects user interaction data, tracking the buttons the player presses on their controller across menus and gameplay, and an AI model looks for input patterns, such as how much time passes between button presses and how system and game menus are interacted with. Sets of inputs are then compared to other stored sets of inputs using a similarity score, which determines if one player is using two different accounts once a certain threshold is passed. An alert is then sent to the platform or the game's developer, who can restrict ranked play or ban the secondary account altogether.

A system like this could lead to false positives, and thus the restricting and banning of legitimate main accounts, but Sony outlined some features in the patent that should reduce the risk. For starters, the AI model can determine the player's skill level by comparing it to other known input sets belonging to high-rank players, and even discard input data that shows when a game has been thrown on purpose to update the system's rating, which will dynamically take into account a player's real performance and update its data accordingly.

While some users may balk at the thought of their input data being given to an AI model, every modern competitive game already records players' input data. Modern fighting games' replays, such as in Street Fighter 6 , rely on input data to recreate the match, so this Sony tech would draw on data already stored for gameplay purposes.

I, for one, would very much welcome a system that deals with smurfing on PlayStation 6 and possibly on every other system. Back in the Street Fighter V days, I admit I did have alternate accounts, but only because the game did not allow me to use secondary characters without tanking the rank of the entire account. However, Street Fighter 6 keeps track of each character's rank separately, solving the issue.

Still, people continue to smurf in competitive games for all sorts of reasons, mostly of the negative sort, so a system like this would go a long way to level the playing field and let newcomers or less experienced players play against those close to their skill rank. The joy of competitive gaming is to improve at any given game, but when the gap in skill level is massive, only frustration remains.

item.title: NVIDIA Vera Delivers 2x The Agent Speed Of AMD’s 256-Core EPYC Venice And 1.6x More Agents Per Watt Than The Frequency-Optimized 96-Core Venice
item.description:
NVIDIA Vera CPUs continue to showcase strong performance and efficiency against leading x86 chips across Agentic AI workloads.

NVIDIA Vera CPU Early Adopters Are Seeing Higher Tool Speed Per Watt, Agentic AI Tasks Per Watt and More Memory/Core Bandwidth Per Watt

The Vera CPU continues to disrupt the Agentic AI segment and has already been adopted by various AI firms. The reason for Vera's adoption at scale is a representation of the ongoing AI demand, which has moved from GPUs to CPUs in the Agentic era.

Agentic AI workloads operate in loops, moving from GPU to CPU and back, often hundreds of times per task. The GPU handles reasoning. The CPU handles the work: tool calls, SQL queries, API calls, scripting, etc. Each loop is sequential and data-hungry, hitting memory again and again.

To keep up with this constant loop, CPUs designed for Agentic AI need to offer:

  • High per-core performance, so tool calls finish quickly
  • High memory bandwidth, so data arrives without delay
  • Low latency, so the next GPU reasoning step starts sooner

NVIDIA's architectural changes within the Vera CPU hit all marks , and the company is sharing new benchmarks which showcase:

  • 1.6x more agents per watt versus the fast x86 96-core part.
  • 2x faster agent speed versus the dense x86 256-core part.

These performance results are compared against AMD's 6th Gen EPYC Venice chips. Against the fastest 6th Gen Venice "Frequency-optimized" SKU with 96 cores, Vera offers 60% higher perf per watt, and against the denser 256-core "Zen 6" SKU, Vera offers twice the agent speed (Tasks per MW).

The results shared by NVIDIA definitely look enticing for Agentic AI customers, and we would like to see a further breakdown from the company. Meanwhile, Vera's adoption across top Agentic AI providers continues to grow, with the early adopters list and their respective production-style test figures shared below:

  • Perplexity: Agentic coding tasks ran 1.5x faster than on traditional CPUs. Perplexity plans to deploy Vera in an upcoming production system.
  • DeepInfra: On its own production agent workload, Vera delivered up to 2.2x the best x86 on agentic orchestration, the fastest of the four architectures tested.
  • ClickHouse: Its standard binary, with no Vera-specific tuning, scaled near-linearly across 176 cores and topped the ClickBench hardware leaderboard.
  • DuckDB: ~1.5x the median TPC-H SF1000 performance of an Intel Xeon 6 baseline.
  • Daytona: 1,000 agent sandboxes online in 10.8 seconds, and 12.7 completed jobs per second at 2,000 concurrent sandboxes, versus 10.9 for AMD EPYC 9755.
  • Modal: Up to 2x sandbox throughput per core versus comparable x86 hardware, with gains that grow under heavy load.

NVIDIA’s Vera CPU is emerging as a practical force in the Agentic AI era, delivering the efficiency and responsiveness these looping, data-intensive workloads demand. Early results from production environments already show it outperforming leading x86 alternatives on both speed and power, reinforcing its growing adoption among AI infrastructure providers.

item.title: Crimson Desert Charting the Unknown Has Performance Issues In Some Areas, But Pearl Abyss Has Finally Started Addressing the Problem in Patch 2.04.08
item.description:
Crimson Desert : Charting the Unknown released last week on PC and consoles, and all those who started venturing into the unknown on their ship have definitely noticed how the expansion is not as polished as the base game. Pearl Abyss was well aware of this, launching a multitude of minor patches and hotfixes to address the most glaring issues. Thankfully, one of the biggest issues - the significant performance drops in some areas - is starting to get addressed in patch 2.04.08 .

"Improved framerate drops in certain areas," is the very first improvement listed on the official patch notes shared by Pearl Abyss today. "We will continue to improve framerate drops that occur in certain situations and during certain content," the Korean developer added to highlight how they will continue to monitor and improve the issue.

As I have spent a good 20 hours playing through the expansion for my review, which will go live in the next few days on PC , I did not encounter any massive performance drops on PC , although I did notice that performance is generally not as stable as it is on the main continent of Pywel . On consoles, however, users have reported significant performance issues, so this patch should have the greatest impact on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S .

Besides addressing performance issues, the new Crimson Desert: Charting the Unknown patch fixes crashing, quest, and naval gameplay issues, including a very immersion-breaking issue where the ship's wheel did not rotate while steering the ship. The full details can be found in the official patch notes .

While my final verdict is still on hold as I continue to explore the new areas, I can already say that Crimson Desert: Charting the Unknown is more than worth the money for those who loved the base game, especially those who got invested in the story after the Enhanced release. The three new epilogue questlines are short, but they are entertaining enough, making Damiane and Oongka feel more like characters and not some gameplay gimmicks thrown in just to spice up the game's combat in certain scenarios.

item.title: XBOX PC App Redesign Rolls Out To Insiders With Up To 60% Faster Launches
item.description:
Microsoft has officially begun rolling out its redesigned XBOX PC app , promising substantial performance improvements and a more streamlined interface. According to the company's latest XBOX Wire announcement , the updated application is up to 60% faster to launch , while navigation and other everyday operations have also received significant optimizations.

This follows our previous coverage in October , when Microsoft was reportedly testing a major overhaul of its XBOX PC app, internally codenamed Garrison . Early hands-on impressions from Windows Central and The Verge's Tom Warren suggested substantially improved responsiveness, particularly when browsing large game libraries .

Microsoft has now provided official figures for the improvements, with Home, Store, and Game Pass pages loading up to 50% faster , while in-app windows reportedly open up to 65% faster . The company emphasizes that these figures are based on internal testing, and actual results will vary depending on hardware configurations, internet connectivity, and other factors .

Beyond performance, the redesigned application introduces a cleaner interface with revamped game cards, refreshed animations, and updated Home and Settings pages . Library navigation has also been simplified, with improved filtering and organization options intended to make managing large game collections less cumbersome .

Social features are now integrated directly into the main navigation , allowing users to see their friends' activity, start conversations, and join parties more conveniently. Meanwhile, an improved unified search function encompasses games, installed titles, downloadable add-ons, and other players .

XBOX chief Asha Sharma also shared a side-by-side demonstration on X of the application's improved responsiveness.

XBOX Cloud Gaming Is Also Receiving A Major Interface Overhaul

Alongside the PC application, Microsoft is expanding its redesigned XBOX Cloud Gaming web experience , which first entered public preview in January .

The revamped interface introduces a consolidated Library for cloud-playable games, including supported purchased titles and XBOX Game Pass offerings . Other additions include improved sorting and filtering, a desktop-optimized layout for larger screens, dark and light themes, and five high-contrast accessibility options .

Microsoft is also bringing similar navigation improvements to XBOX Cloud Gaming applications on supported televisions and VR headsets , seeking greater consistency across its gaming ecosystem.

The updated XBOX PC app began rolling out to XBOX Insiders on November 5 , while the refreshed web experience is expanding to more users over the coming weeks. Microsoft has not specified a general release date for the redesigned PC application .

Although these improvements address several longstanding complaints about Microsoft's PC gaming software, whether the redesign can meaningfully narrow the usability gap with competing storefronts such as Steam remains to be seen.

News Source: XBOX Wire

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Modders Add a Training Dummy, 1600 Foes Survival Mode, and Roguelite-Style Mode, as S-Game’s First Patch Brings No Major Gameplay Additions
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero launched last week on PC and PlayStation 5 , and it's a rather polished release that has no glaring issues. However, S-Game has already released the first patch to iron out some kinks and introduce new features. In terms of new gameplay features, however, the development studio has yet to add anything significant, leaving it to modders to fill some of the gaps, making the experience even more engaging on PC even for those who already saw the end of Soul's journey.

Unofficial Training Mode

One gripe I had during my first playthrough (which was not enough to move the needle from the 10/10 score the game rightly deserved in my opinion) was how enemies do not respawn , preventing me from trying out and practicing with all of the game's incredible weapons. A training mode would have served as well, but the game also doesn't feature one.

With the DPS Dummy mod , however, Phantom Blade Zero finally gets one in the form of a dummy enemy that blends into the environment near the Outpost fast-travel point. As the mod displays "DPS, total damage, last-hit damage and time to empty the health bar," and automatically restores Soul's health and Sha-Chi when he stops attacking, it is the best unofficial implementation possible of a proper training mode.

New Challenging Encounters

In terms of endgame content, Phantom Blade Zero definitely doesn't disappoint, as the 66-Days mode adds a layer of tension to the experience that forces the player to master the game's combat mechanics, a tension that rises with every New Game+ cycle that increases enemy stats. However, if you're willing to further put your skills to the test without having to replay through the entire game again and again, The HexTower and Phantom Master Ninja are mods you should definitely try out.

"Ring the bell to start HexTower. Pick a route through three acts, fight elites, and build your run with augments and relics. Visit shops and campfires before each act boss. Boss Rush and a Training Camp are also available," reads the official description of the HexTower mod on Nexus Mods . This mod essentially adds something akin to a roguelite mode where players build Soul with additional augments as he takes on several combat challenges. While simple on paper, this idea works wonders thanks to the game's excellent combat design, and the built-in Boss Rush mode leverages the incredible boss design to let players take them on repeatedly and refine their builds to the next level.

While much simpler in execution, the Phantom Master Ninja mod adds even more of a challenge in the form of a survival mode. "Built specifically for hardcore fans of Ninja Gaiden 2 on Master Ninja difficulty, Phantom Master Ninja throws you into relentless survival gauntlets with up to 24 aggressive enemies on screen simultaneously and wave totals from 160 to 1,600 enemies," reads the mod's description on Nexus Mods . "Test your mastery in any region across difficulties ranging from Hellwalker to NG+6. Unless you are a Ninja Dog, prepare for relentless action." The mod also comes with additional settings to tweak the challenge level, which are a definitive plus for those who may not be ready for the relentless vanilla settings.

With weapons having very diverse playstyles, these additional Phantom Blade Zero challenges are the perfect way to delve deeper into one of the best action RPGs of the generation. We still don't know if S-Game plans to add something similar officially down the line, but the game's future still looks bright.

item.title: Windows 11 27H2 Could Be The Biggest Windows Upgrade Since 2024, With Major Performance Improvements And New Wallpapers
item.description:
Microsoft is reportedly preparing a major Windows 11 overhaul for 2027, prioritizing performance and reliability over launching Windows 12 .

Microsoft is reportedly preparing a substantial Windows 11 upgrade for 2027, potentially making version 27H2 the operating system's biggest update since 24H2 in 2024 . The company is also developing new default wallpapers , while its broader efforts to improve Windows performance continue.

According to The Verge's Tom Warren , Microsoft intends to make Windows 11 27H2 a full operating system upgrade , replacing or substantially updating core components rather than simply enabling features already present on users' PCs.

Windows 11 27H2 Could Introduce Major Under-The-Hood Changes

This would mark a departure from Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, both delivered through relatively small enablement packages. As Microsoft officially explained , these versions share an underlying servicing platform, allowing upgrades through small downloads and a single restart on eligible systems .

Windows 11 27H2 would instead resemble the more extensive 24H2 transition, potentially requiring more comprehensive compatibility testing. The report also suggests that Windows Insider testing could begin earlier than usual in 2027 .

Performance improvements are expected to remain a major priority. Microsoft recently announced that its latest optimizations make Windows 11 up to 20% more responsive and multitasking up to 40% faster on systems with 8GB of RAM, according to internal measurements.

These improvements are already available on supported Windows 11 26H2 installations rather than being exclusive to the upcoming 27H2 release. Nevertheless, they illustrate Microsoft's renewed emphasis on operating system efficiency.

Another potentially significant development concerns Intel's Advanced Performance Extensions (APX) . As we previously reported , experimental Windows 11 builds have begun exposing APX support, which could improve performance in appropriately optimized 64-bit applications on compatible future processors.

APX doubles the number of general-purpose CPU registers from 16 to 32 , potentially reducing memory operations and instruction overhead. However, Microsoft has not confirmed that APX will ship with Windows 11 27H2, and the benefits will depend on hardware and software support.

New Default Wallpapers, But Windows 12 May Have To Wait

Beyond the underlying improvements, Microsoft is reportedly preparing to replace Windows 11's familiar Bloom wallpaper with a series of new designs, potentially unveiled during Microsoft Ignite 2026 later this month.

The new wallpapers reportedly feature folded, colorful shapes surrounded by clouds, with variations for consumer and commercial editions. Consumer designs could reflect gaming, productivity, creativity, and performance , while Windows 11 Pro would retain a color scheme closer to the original Bloom aesthetic.

A broader wallpaper rollout is reportedly planned for January 2027 , ahead of the operating system's major annual update.

Interestingly, the report also suggests that Microsoft is focusing on improving Windows 11 rather than introducing Windows 12 next year . The company has not officially ruled out a new Windows version, however.

For now, Windows 11 27H2 looks increasingly likely to emphasize fundamental improvements in performance, reliability, and the overall user experience , although its final features, hardware requirements, and precise release date remain unconfirmed.

News Source: The Verge

item.title: NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang Summoned By U.S. Congress For A Closed Door Briefing To Address His Interactions With An Executive That’s In The Federal Spy Probe’s Crosshairs
item.description:
NVIDIA has spent the last several years trying to balance its status as the world’s dominant force in artificial intelligence with strict United States export regulations. Unfortunately, these efforts might not have borne fruit as the company’s CEO, Jensen Huang, now finds himself as the latest target of congressional investigators over potentially sensitive national security vulnerabilities.

A coalition of U.S. House Republicans has formally requested that NVIDIA’s head honcho appear on Capitol Hill for a joint, closed door briefing to address foreign adversary espionage, which has materialized thanks to his interactions with a Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, who is currently a suspected People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset.

China has recently obtained access to sensitive U.S. technology; a letter signed by three lawmakers wants to question Jensen Huang

The official request, sent on November 4, 2026, was signed by Representative Brian Mast (Chairman of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs), Representative John Moolenaar (Chairman of the House Select Committee on the CCP), and Representative Rick Crawford (Chairman of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence).

The lawmakers are seeking to question Huang about NVIDIA’s security protocols designed to prevent foreign-adversary espionage, as well as his past interactions with Alice Huang. The Megaspeed executive has been under United States government surveillance for supposedly feeding technology information to the Chinese government.

Given that a security research firm discovered that 32 of NVIDIA’s B300 GPUs, which are on the U.S. export control list, were seemingly deployed at China Telecom , it highlights that the trillion-dollar firm’s most advanced chips are finding their way overseas. The joint letter from the three chairmen expressed severe concerns over how much sensitive technology might be making its way into the hands of the Chinese state, noting that PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology sit at the heart of their investigative priorities.

The aforementioned GPUs also rely on HBM to deliver unrivaled inference performance, and, as you’ve already guessed, High Bandwidth Memory from top manufacturers like Samsung and SK hynix cannot be exported to China. Fortunately, smugglers found an incredible loophole where throwaway server chips equipped with HBM were rerouted from Hong Kong to China, then de-soldered to be re-purposed for different applications .

The congressional chairmen have requested that Huang appear in Room 2172 of the Rayburn House Office Building on November 18, 2026, to brief their committees, asking for acceptance of the date or a proposed alternative by November 11, 2026. The briefing could mark a critical moment for NVIDIA as the U.S. continues to restrict Chinese access to advanced semiconductor hardware, but as previous events have shown, there’s always a way for rivals to obtain the newest silicon.

  • 21-40%: Questionable - Some concerns remain

Timeline 4/5

The two biggest parties in the consortium that bought Electronic Arts for $55 billion , Silver Lake and Saudi Arabia's PIF , are back in business and trying to acquire Unity .

The big news comes from Reuters , which claims that Silver Lake and PIF approached Unity's management about the possibility in recent weeks . Silver Lake and PIF reportedly evaluated Unity at about $25 billion , though that was before Unity's latest earnings report, which lifted its market ​capitalization to around $21.5 billion.

Reuters adds that since the consortium approached Unity, the company, originally founded in Denmark and now headquartered in San Francisco, has been evaluating its options with the help of an investment bank . No deal has been reached so far, anyway.

Unity was founded twenty-two years ago and is best known for its Unity engine , a popular cross-platform game engine. In fact, there are more games made with this engine (especially on mobile) than on Epic's Unreal Engine , although the latter is generally preferred by triple-A developers for its more advanced rendering capabilities. Unity used to be an indie favorite, but that partly changed after 2023's runtime fee fiasco , which led to former CEO John Riccitiello 's eventual resignation . Recently, Unity has gone all-in on AI integration , though Epic is doing the same with Unreal.

As mentioned earlier, Silver Lake and PIF recently acquired Electronic Arts, with the help of a third investor, Affinity Partners. However, Affinity Partners only holds 1.1% of the company, while Silver Lake owns 5.5% of EA and PIF owns the rest (93.4%). Silver Lake actually invested in Unity back in 2017 and already owns 8% of the company's shares , which would certainly facilitate a deal.

The gaming community watches with wariness, especially after their acquisition of EA ostensibly led to the closure of historic developer BioWare , a massive blow to RPG fans worldwide.

item.title: Meta Exec Says A Recently Elected, Data Center-Skeptic Democratic Governor Now Wants To Meet After Inauguration, As 22.5 GW Of Capacity Is Still Slated To Come Online Regardless Of Politics
item.description:
Some say the AI bubble has just popped, especially given the carnage unfolding across wide swathes of the market today. Many point to the Democratic sweep on Tuesday, and the ensuing likelihood of a broad-based moratorium on data center construction. And yet, a dispassionate analysis of this paradigm yields a relatively benign picture, one that posits that tens of gigawatts of new capacity would still come online in 2027.

Over 20 GW of under-construction data centers have achieved 75 percent completion rates, requiring only equipment installations and power

First, let's discuss how the wheels seem to have suddenly come off the AI gravy train. OpenAI is now discussing dampening its compute buildout cadence after 40 percent of its planned capacity additions for 2027 suddenly became stranded in Democrat-controlled states - Texas, Ohio, Georgia, and New Mexico.

OpenAI has also separately declared that it will not demand NDAs when dealing with public officials , will pay the full cost of electricity and grid infrastructure, and publicly disclose its water and power consumption.

Elsewhere, Microsoft has just increased the scrutiny of its neocloud partners - including Nebius, IREN and Nscale - amid threats to its AI infrastructure buildout plans.

As we noted recently , Texas is particularly important for the ongoing AI buildout, especially as the state accounts for ~25 percent of the planned US data center capacity by 2030 , replete with a large-load power queue that now spans 474 gigawatts , as tabulated by the Electric Reliability Council Of Texas (ERCOT).

Against this backdrop, the governor-elect of Texas, Gina Hinojosa (D), is attracting a fair share of consternation within the AI sphere, especially as she has already called for zero subsidies for data centers, unionized labor, no NDAs, and the furnishing of proof that the buildout won't increase household water and power bills .

This brings us to the core of today's topic. Meta's President, Dina Powell McCormick, declared to the Wall Street Journal just today that a newly elected Democratic governor, who had made data centers a campaign issue, has approached Meta for a meetup after their inauguration as they " don't want these jobs to go elsewhere ."

This suggests that the situation is not as dire as presumed by many, and that there remains a substantial room for coming to an amicable agreement on the cadence of AI infrastructure buildout.

Do note that Meta's CapEx was, until recently, expected to hit a whopping $145 billion in 2027, spanning projects such as Louisiana's Hyperion (in partnership with BlackRock), Ohio's Prometheus, and a third site in Texas. Meta is also looking at offshore data center opportunities.

McCormick did concede that new projects are expected to face "more scrutiny" going forward, while expanding existing campuses will remain a far easier task, especially as local communities around established campuses enjoy a myriad of benefits, including a large number of jobs and investments.

Meanwhile, as per a separate analysis by Aterio, as of November 05, around 86.7 GW of US data centers remain under construction, with around 50 GW at vertical construction or beyond, which basically means that the shell has been erected, while 22.5 GW of capacity is at or above 75 percent completion rate , requiring only equipment installations and power connections.

Critically, moratoria on data center constructions won't necessarily affect this 22.5 GW slice of upcoming capacity, especially as operators can deploy behind-the-meter solutions such as gas turbines or Bloom Energy's natural gas-based fuel cells.

What's more, Hinojosa has declared that all data centers already authorized within Texas will be allowed to complete their construction phase . This covers almost all of the capacity expected to come online in 2027. For data centers that debut in 2028/2029, Hinojosa is now demanding the withdrawal of subsidies, unionized labor, the furnishing of proof that the buildout won't increase household water and power bills, and a seat at the proverbial table for Texans.

So, there you have it. Moratoria on data center constructions will not prevent 22.5 GW of capacity that is already in advanced stages of completion from coming online. This capacity is large enough to satisfy incremental compute needs through 2028. Hardly a reason for the wild convulsions in the AI sphere today!

item.title: Data Centers Aren’t Ready For The Next AI Bottleneck; Power Infrastructure, As NVIDIA’s Kyber Racks Could Require Electricity Usage Equivalent To 500 Homes
item.description:
AI hardware has continued to evolve at a dizzying pace over the past few years, resulting in creating misery for consumers as far as the DRAM shortage goes, but there could be an even bigger problem on the horizon that data centers or governments simply aren’t equipped to handle; addressing the power infrastructure. As frontier AI models demand larger clusters to be trained on, the power density is scaling to mind-boggling heights.

The latest visual data highlights NVIDIA’s upcoming Kyber rack system, built around the Rubin Ultra NVL576 platform , and the numbers reveal a looming crisis for enterprise server farms. Here’s the figure that’ll knock your socks off; a single Kyber rack will require an astonishing 600kW of continuous electricity, making it equivalent to the power draw of roughly 500 average American households

Server racks in 2024 only required 8kW, making NVIDIA’s Kyber system a menace when it comes to guzzling power requirements

An estimation in the form of a graph was shared by Jessie Dong showing the exponential rise in power consumption across successive NVIDIA GPU architectures, painting a grim picture regarding the direction of power requirements for high-performance computing. To remind you, in 2022, a typical high-density NVIDIA Hopper rack consumed roughly 40kW. By 2024, the Blackwell NVL72 architecture pushed that limit to around 120kW.

With Kyber slated to arrive in the second half of 2027, power requirements will leap to a mammoth 600kW per cabinet, resulting in a staggering 5x increase over Blackwell and pulling 75 times more juice than a standard 8kW enterprise server rack. With the memory shortage, the primary players can simply raise their production capacity over several years, addressing demand to some extent, but this is a whole new league of problems.

Supplying this level of electricity is far more nuanced than simply securing grid capacity from local utility providers. Modern data center operators are encountering severe internal delivery bottlenecks because retrofitting existing facilities to deliver 600kW directly to individual rack footprints is practically impossible. Amazon is estimated to have already paid $5 billion in GB300 rack deliveries , but it has no way to power these AI GPUs because the infrastructure is simply unprepared to handle such a load.

The problem doesn’t stop at Amazon either, because the largest AI labs always snap up the newest architectures first, meaning data center operators hoping to capture frontier AI revenues must first construct purpose-built facilities from the ground up. We’ve previously reported in 2025 that the AI data center boom is so massive that the national power grid is in a bottleneck state , and with 600kW of juice required, a major warning is being sent to hyperscalers.

Unless future data centers are completely re-architected from the power mains to the cooling manifolds, the next wave of generative AI will find itself stranded without enough power to boot.

item.title: NVIDIA’s Vendor Financing Deals Are Not A Ponzi Scheme As It Is Slated To “Take Out $420 Billion” By Putting In $250 Billion, Says Tech Venture Capitalist Gene Munster
item.description:
Technology venture capitalist Gene Munster believes that NVIDIA's financing deals, through which the firm lends to its customers to enable them to establish their AI infrastructure, are not a Ponzi scheme. Munster made the remarks during the Zero Hedge podcast, where he compared the deals to the environment in the Dotcom bubble era of the 90s and pointed out the differences.

Gene Munster Says Circular Contracts Of The 90s Aren't Similar To NVIDIA's Capital Financing Deals Because Of Massive Future Upside

NVIDIA's vendor financing agreements, which the firm has outlined are worth at least $108.5 billion, involve it helping some customers to pick their data center sites that are capable of supporting the demand for its products. The $108.5 billion figure c omes from NVIDIA's latest quarterly SEC filings , but the firm has been rumored to have aimed much higher.

This figure, $250 billion, came courtesy of a report from The Wall Street Journal in late July, which outlined that NVIDIA was in discussions with OpenAI to guarantee the figure as part of backstop agreements. Yet, the firm's SEC filings indicate that $105 billion of the $108.5 billion disclosed figure was tied to a site in Ohio which OpenAI is developing.

Discussing the deals, which have come under criticism as being circular in nature and propping up the demand for NVIDIA's products, venture capitalist Gene Munster dismissed comparisons with the Dotcom bubble of the 90s. When asked during the Zero Hedge podcast about vendor financing in the 90s, he started off by dismissing the contracts as vendor financing and called them circular instead.

Munster then added:

"Where companies would raise money they would spend money on other companies. These are ad driven businesses, a lot of the initial internet businesses. It was like, basically one business raising money, propping up another business. A partnership and they did it until that capital ran out and then there was no buyer for the ads. So that got us to 2000."

However, he called the NVIDIA deals "totally logical" and not a Ponzi scheme. Referring to the rumored figure, outlining that while the firm had committed "like 250 billion," it was slated to make almost twice as much. The commitment is part of a package with major financiers such as BlackRock and Apollo Global, Munster said.

Explaining further, he outlined:

"That pool is about a trillion dollars. NVIDIA, so if we put NVIDIA out as the group that is causing this Ponzi scheme, it's totally logical for NVIDIA to do this. NVIDIA is going to take 60% of that revenue. They have, call it, 70% gross margin. They will put in 250 billion. They will take out 420 billion. What is a Ponzi scheme about that? That is just smart business."

item.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla Update 1.8.0 Adds More Than NG+, Raising Divine Gear’s Upgrade Cap From 13 to 27 and Introducing 300+ Engravable Runes
item.description:
As promised in last week's franchise-wide update , Ubisoft has now released Update 1.8.0 for Assassin's Creed Valhalla . Its size varies quite a bit depending on the platform:

  • Ubisoft Connect: 12.27 GB
  • Steam: 7.8 GB
  • Xbox Series X|S: 15.02 GB
  • PlayStation 5: 5.26 GB
  • PlayStation 4: 13.42 GB
  • Xbox One: 13.8 GB

The patch's highlight is, of course, the long-awaited addition of the New Game Plus mode . Players can begin a new playthrough with their existing character progress after they have completed the Holy Day Quest , which is the last quest of the Hamtunscire region. This isn't quite at the point of the game's true ending, but given the gargantuan size of Assassin's Creed Valhalla, the developers decided to allow players to start their NG+ adventures a little earlier.

The team also explained that in NG+, obtaining gear you already own or interacting with a Book of Knowledge you have already acquired will grant a new source called Mithril . Mithril will also be available from the Niflheim, Mastery, and River Raid shops, giving players who wish to continue their endgame adventure another source of materials. In addition, Wealth Chests that would normally contain Carbon, Nickel, or Tungsten will instead award Platinum, an ingot previously exclusive to the Dawn of Ragnarok DLC , now available for free. As a result, upgrading gear to Divine quality will no longer require that DLC .

Each iteration of NG+ will get tougher , and Ubisoft promises worthy challenges for players. To keep up with them, the developers have increased the maximum upgrade level for every piece of Divine gear from 13 to 27 , giving gear even more potential power. Upgrades will now require the new Mithril resource, so players will need plenty of that.

Moreover, Ubisoft introduced an Extended Progression Mode that is designed to provide a more granular sense of progression. When enabled, Gear upgrades and Runes will increase Power by 1 point, and Masteries increase Power every 5 skill points, thus increasing the impact of gear .

The Rune Forge has received a substantial update, too : players will find a new tab in the menu where they can upgrade runes using silver. Runes can be upgraded from lesser to normal, then normal to greater, and finally from greater to superior, a new tier available only through the rune upgrade page. The final upgrade costs Mithril instead of silver and gives players even more power from their runes.

The Rune Forge's second addition is to the engrave page, which now offers more than 300 runes to engrave . Players can use it to engrave every perk added since Assassin's Creed Valhalla launched, including perks from DLCs and the Helix Store. Once players acquire a weapon or a full armor set, they'll find it in the engrave menu and can turn it into a rune for 450 silver. T his opens up lots of new perk combinations , according to Ubisoft.

Lastly, the update adds a Stash in Ravensthorpe, which allows players to store any piece of gear and any rune from their inventory.

Update 1.8.0 for Assassin's Creed Valhalla also implements native PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) 2.0 , enhancing image quality on PlayStation 5 Pro consoles.

Assassin's Creed Valhalla is the best-performing game in the series, having surpassed a billion in revenue in February 2022 , just fifteen months after launch. Most recently, Ubisoft said the game had registered over 40 million players to date.
