item.title: Acer Technician Ruined A Gaming Laptop’s Liquid Metal Application With A Knife And Completely Forgot About Pasting The CPU, Leaving It Throttling At 105°C
item.description:
Applying liquid metal to gaming laptops is always a nerve-wracking experience, even more so when a qualified technician ends up botching the job on premium machines like the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI. One customer describes his experience as a nightmare because, in an attempt to resolve his gaming laptop’s thermal throttling, the company personnel not only forgot to apply paste to the CPU, but also used a knife to spread the paste on the GPU. Needless to say, the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI continued to overheat.

Lack of technician training can result in improper gaming laptop servicing, but owners should also be mindful of what company employees are up to

The experience was detailed by Redditor ‘u/egoxvert,’ as his Predator Helios Neo 16S AI featuring an Intel Core Ultra 7 255HX CPU and an NVIDIA RTX 5060 GPU was hitting temperatures of 105°C and 87°C, respectively. After waiting an entire month for Acer’s warranty support to respond, which only occurred after lodging a formal grievance on the National Consumer Helpline, a technician finally arrived at the customer’s home to inspect the laptop

Rather than delivering a professional repair job, the technician appeared completely out of his depth from the moment the rear panel was unscrewed. According to the owner, the worker immediately called a supervisor to ask if there was a tutorial video explaining how to apply liquid metal to a gaming laptop. After cleaning off the factory compound, the technician merely squeezed two drops of liquid metal directly onto the GPU die and attempted to slap the heatsink back in place, skipping the mandatory step of spreading the compound evenly across the die.

Anyone rocking these machines knows that liquid metal is electrically conductive, and failing to contain and spread the material properly can create massive hot spots and pose a severe risk of short-circuiting nearby components if it spills over the barrier. The situation worsened when the customer asked if the CPU thermal interface had also been renewed. Realizing he completely forgot the processor, the technician removed the heatsink once again, pulled out an unbranded tub of paste, scooped up a thick lump using a knife, and slapped it onto the CPU die without spreading it.

Unsurprisingly, the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI didn’t escape its thermal throttling woes, with the CPU and GPU temperatures retained at 105°C and 87°C. The owner isn’t the first to experience firsthand a botched liquid metal application job as a Lenovo technician rendered an RTX 4090-powered Legion 7i completely useless thanks to subpar servicing. To make matters worse, Lenovo didn’t even offer a replacement unit . After hearing about the aftermath of liquid metal on PS5 units , we’ve come to the conclusion that PTM7950 is a far safer and better alternative.

With a PTM7950 sheet in the 80mm x 80mm x 0.25mm dimensions going for just $23.99 on places like Amazon , it’s a great idea to take the less destructive approach and stop allowing unskilled technicians to work on your expensive hardware.

item.title: TSMC’s 1-nanometer Chip Making Site Could Be In A Science Park That Also Manufactures Components For Space Use Imply Taiwanese Official’s Statements
item.description:
After his earlier comments discussing potential plans for TSMC's 1-nanometer chip production factory, the chairman of Taiwan's National Science Council, Cheng-Weng Wu, has discussed details about resource planning at the Nanke Sharon Park in Tainan, Taiwan. The minister's comments had hinted that the 1-nanometer site might be located in the Tainan region at the IEEE Asia Solid State Circuits Conference and his latest remarks, as per the Taiwanese media, were made in Taiwan's parliament.

Taiwan's Technology Council Minister Shares Tainan Science Park Could Also Target Sub-1-nanometer Chip Manufacturing Process Technologies

TSMC's 1-nanometer technology, which is dubbed the A10, is perhaps among the most advanced manufacturing technologies the firm has disclosed to date. In 2023, at the IEDM conference, the firm shared that by 2030 it could be able to cram a whopping 200 billion transistors in a monolithic die. A monolithic die is a single chip manufactured without combining multiple dies to increase transistor density and offering superior performance due to a lack of signal loss and other factors.

More recently, at the 2026 Europe Technology Symposium, TSMC shared plans for processes stretching as far out as the A12 manufacturing process, which was slated for production in 2029. The firm shared that the A14 platform, or the 1.4-nanometer technology, would enable development of A13 and A12 and A12 would enable it to adopt backside power delivery .

Now, after a 2025 report from the UDN in Taiwan claimed that TSMC could build a 1-nanometer fab at the Shalun Park in Tainan, Taiwan, Taiwan's head of the National Science Council, Cheng-Wen Wu, has confirmed that a 1-nanometer chip manufacturing site will be located in the region. Wu's comments come after his earlier remarks that had hinted at a similar site in the Tainan region.

As per the UDN , in the Taiwanese parliament, he shared that feasibility assessment and resource planning for the new technology park in Shalun had been completed and the second phase of the environmental assessment was currently underway.

He added that the park was not only being developed for 1-nanometer manufacturing sites but also for technologies that are more advanced. Wu also outlined that other high-growth technologies, such as robotics, would also play a role in the region.

The Taiwanese official's remarks built on his earlier comments where he had outlined that the growth in high technology areas such as robotics would enable traditionally low-value materials companies to serve the high-value supply chain. This time, he also added space into the mix and asserted that as long as the firms in the Shalun park maintained quality standards, their products could also go to space.
